analysis:
Examined all four supplied analyses and the available source replay. Replay is incomplete (23 of 25 source units omitted), so this integration cannot independently validate the duplicate requant.py:406 path-traversal candidates. They remain unresolved, not disproved: retrieve scripts/models/requant.py:343–419 and check whether downloaded template paths can escape the output root before candidate verification.

The visible .github/workflows/model-requant-upload.yml enforces master-ref checks (105–113, 148–156), pinned checkout without persisted credentials, hash-required binary dependencies, quantizer selftests, prod-environment placement, and environment-based quoted input handling. Reconstruction and verification precede credentialed upload (244–282). No concrete regression is established by this YAML or the ci-master.yml:175–177 offline-test addition. Environment reviewer/bypass configuration is an external contract, not demonstrated enforcement. Historical repository-secret accessibility is not a new regression.

Material remaining review: inspect scripts/models/upload-model-revision.py for URL/path validation, safe workflow-output emission, complete byte verification, immutable reservation and overwrite prevention. In particular, upstream validation of the candidate manifest does not necessarily validate the separately downloaded template manifest. A reconstruction-time arbitrary write could compromise subsequent verification or credentialed execution in the same job even though secrets are step-scoped. Inspect requant.py remote reads, redirects and resource bounds, and the omitted tests. The new remote-model-data → CI filesystem → credentialed publication boundary warrants threat-model coverage, relevant to A-004, T-012, T-027 and T-007. Publication remains visibly separate from registration/promotion; no supplied runtime change alters authorization, attestation, hop encryption, billing or T-041 cache isolation. This limited result does not clear the earlier candidate finding.
